PullRequest.Title: Automations: Add CRON schedule support
PullRequest.Body:
## Motivation Automations currently expose only preset schedules, which makes recurring workflows with more precise timing impossible to configure without losing trigger details. This PR adds validated five-field CRON schedules across Agent Host persistence, the create/edit flow, automation tools, cards, and accessibility surfaces while preserving existing trigger data exactly. This PR exposes the scheduling grammar already supported by the Agent Host Protocol; it does not extend host syntax or negotiate new capabilities.

## Changes made - Uses **CRON** consistently in the trigger picker, expression label, cards, errors, and accessibility text; protocol identifiers remain lowercase. - Validation errors identify the field without appending the invalid input. Step errors provide an explicitly valid range example, such as `0-59` for minutes. - Adds five-field Agent Host CRON schedules using the existing AHP grammar: names, lists, ascending ranges, positive steps on `*` or an explicit range, and Sunday aliases. For example, `20-59/15` selects minutes 20, 35, and 50. - Rejects starting-value shorthand such as `20/15` with an inline error and disabled Save. Tools reject it before approval/mutation, and blueprint imports reject it. Unsupported expressions are never silently rewritten or sent as accepted schedules. - Keeps month constraints outside the inclusive union of restricted day-of-month and weekday fields. The live explanation puts the month first to avoid ambiguity. - Adds a segmented editor spanning two schedule tracks beside a one-track Trigger, local-time guidance, focused field help, and a live human-readable summary. - Supports native caret movement, whole-expression selection, clipboard ingress, and Escape dismissal without losing the draft. - Round trips raw expressions and IANA zones through tools and Agent Host storage, preserving trigger identity and policy on unrelated edits. Local-time blueprints reject foreign-zone export they cannot preserve. - Keeps Cloud CRON unavailable in the UI and explicitly rejected by tools; GitHub Actions documentation is not evidence that the separate Copilot Cloud Automation API supports it. ## Validation Latest error-copy and CRON-capitalization revision, run in the isolated worktree using `fnm exec --using 24.22.1 --`:

- Verified uppercase visible and ARIA expression labels, picker text, saved-card labels, accessible schedule text, and user-facing errors. Lowercase wire/API identifiers and grammar remain unchanged. - Exact-message regressions cover field-specific range examples and removal of invalid-input suffixes; the errors still block Save and unsupported tool mutations. - Matched real production-form fixtures captured Before/After for the error cleanup and capitalization. The existing OSS window and draft were not touched; no real automation was created or run. - The protocol-only restriction was previously verified with 364 browser and 212 Node tests and an 82-case comparison against the exact pre-PR host parser. Its client typecheck passed. These broader checks were not repeated solely for copy changes. - Historical clipboard evidence: eight trusted headless production-fixture checks invoked actual shared Copy/Cut actions and native clipboard events using a minimal test menu host, not the full platform/native-OS menu service. - Historical independent reviews: two GPT-6 Astra contexts reviewed the feature and changed-chunk deltas through `48771bf2fcd`; not rerun for these later scoped revisions. - Electron, broad typecheck, full-PR coverage, and a fresh live-OSS walkthrough were not rerun for this copy-only revision. Hosted CI and review status remain separate from local test results. ### Intentional and inherited differences - **Protocol scope:** starting-value shorthand such as `20/15`, `MAR/3`, and `MON/2` is intentionally unsupported. Use an existing AHP wildcard/range step such as `*/15` or `20-59/15`. This PR does not add wire normalization or new host-language capabilities. - Local schedules retain local-time defaults and per-minute support; GitHub Actions service defaults/interval limits are not imported. - AHP weekdays remain 0–7, with both 0 and 7 representing Sunday. No new implicit weekday-step semantics are introduced. - Existing Agent Host DST policy is unchanged: nonexistent fixed local times are skipped, and repeated times can match twice. This is not exact GitHub-app catch-up/once-only runtime parity. - The actual GitHub-app frontend was executed for syntax/reference comparisons; its pinned Rust backend was source-inspected, not executed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous call chain is explicit: AutomationCronInput.changed() validates before firing onDidChange; this added callback validates again before describeAutomationCron and then calls revalidate(), whose updateSaveButtonState validates a third time. describeAutomationCron reparses and creates uncached locale formatters. Exact device cost is unmeasured, but the repeated UI-thread mechanism and per-keystroke reachability are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UI-thread CPU, Intl.DateTimeFormat objects, Date objects, parsed sets and temporary strings
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The full chain runs once for every input event while editing a CRON field; work also grows with the number of values represented by list/range fields when descriptions format those values.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased input latency and potential typing jank in the automation dialog
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR the dialog had no CRON editor or live CRON description, so typing in the automation form did not execute this parser/formatter chain.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every CRON edit now synchronously validates inside AutomationCronInput, validates again in updateCronDescription, reparses and formats the description, then revalidates the whole form and the CRON expression again.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added onDidChange path calls updateCronDescription(), whose added line 1235 invokes describeAutomationCron(expression), and then revalidate(). The new AutomationCronInput.changed() already calls validate(), while updateSaveButtonState's added cronError assignment performs the third validation.
Findings.Title: Coalesce CRON parsing and description work per edit
Findings.Impact: Typing or using arrow keys in a valid CRON expression can stall feedback and caret handling, especially on lower-end machines or for list-heavy expressions, because multiple ICU formatter constructions and duplicate parses occur on every key event.
Findings.Evidence: getAutomationCronValidationError calls validateAutomationCron, which parses and constructs an Intl.DateTimeFormat. describeAutomationCron reparses and creates fresh safeIntl DateTimeFormat instances; safeIntl.DateTimeFormat returns a new Lazy each call, so these are not shared. It also builds hourDescription and weekDays eagerly even when the final branch says every hour/every day. Thus a valid keystroke performs four parses and several formatter constructions synchronously before returning to the browser event loop.
Findings.Recommendation: Parse/validate once per changed value and pass that result to both the input error state, form validity, and description generation. Cache locale formatters and compute only the description branches needed; if description formatting remains nontrivial, coalesce it to one deferred update while keeping validation immediate.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The catalog derived observable maps every entry through _projectAutomation/projectSchedule on each catalog change, and the added condition constructs Intl.DateTimeFormat before distinguishing hourly, daily, weekly, or weekdays. The exact automation counts and formatter duration vary, but the O(N) repeated construction and synchronous refresh path are directly established.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Intl.DateTimeFormat instances and associated ICU initialization CPU/objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One uncached formatter is constructed for each single-trigger canonical schedule on every catalog projection, so cost grows linearly with the number of visible Agent Host automations and repeats on catalog updates.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: higher synchronous catalog refresh latency and avoidable allocation/GC pressure
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before the diff, hourly, daily, and weekly schedules returned before resolving the local time zone; only the weekdays branch constructed Intl.DateTimeFormat for this comparison.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The local-time-zone comparison is now placed before preset parsing, so every otherwise representable hourly, daily, weekly, and weekdays schedule constructs its own formatter during projection.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1210 calls Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone in the common pre-parse guard. _projectAutomations maps every catalog entry through projectSchedule, whereas the deleted implementation performed this check only inside the weekdays branch.
Findings.Title: Resolve the local time zone once per catalog projection
Findings.Impact: Opening or refreshing the Automations view for a host with many schedules does avoidable serial ICU initialization on the UI thread, delaying card updates and adding short-lived allocation pressure whenever the catalog changes.
Findings.Evidence: AgentHostAutomationStore.automations is a derived value invalidated by _catalog.onDidChange; _projectAutomations maps catalog.entries and _projectAutomation calls projectSchedule for each. No formatter or local-zone cache exists in this path. Intl.DateTimeFormat construction is synchronous and substantially heavier than comparing the resulting time-zone string.
Findings.Recommendation: Resolve the local time zone once at the start of _projectAutomations and pass it into projectSchedule (with a one-off default for direct getAutomation calls), so system time-zone changes remain observable while each catalog refresh performs one formatter construction rather than one per entry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the automation dialog and edit a CRON expression
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dialog rendering eagerly creates the five segmented InputBox controls even for preset schedules. Once CRON is selected, each browser input event synchronously validates, updates the live description, and revalidates the form before caret/input feedback can complete; no boundary call is involved in the edit path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Five fixed input controls at dialog open; while editing, cost scales with input-event frequency and with the number of values in list/range fields used to build the description.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All work is serialized on the browser UI event loop. There is no debounce, deferred render, or coalescing between validation, description generation, and whole-form validation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no parsed-expression cache or formatter cache. The same expression is parsed four times on a valid edit, and safeIntl returns fresh lazy formatter instances for each description call. Empty input exits validation early, while every valid nonempty edit is a cold path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the input event call chain, repeated validation calls, uncached formatter construction, and UI-thread placement are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Intl/ICU construction time varies by platform and locale, and five eager InputBoxes alone may be modest; the duplicate synchronous parser/formatter work per keystroke is nevertheless established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression: live CRON editing adds repeated parser and locale-formatting work to every valid keystroke.

Scenarios.Scenario: Receive an Agent Host automation catalog update and render automation cards
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The pre-existing catalog subscription delivers an update, then the derived automations observable synchronously maps every catalog entry through _projectAutomation/projectSchedule before consumers receive the refreshed list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to and receive Agent Host AutomationCatalog state changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One long-lived subscription and one incoming state event per catalog update; there is no per-automation IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscription and event cardinality existed, but hourly/daily/weekly projection returned before constructing a local-time-zone formatter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The IPC event precedes synchronous projection; the newly repeated formatter work delays publication after the event arrives.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of non-history Agent Host automation entries in the catalog; one new Intl.DateTimeFormat construction occurs for each canonical single-trigger schedule during each projection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Projection is a serial array map on the renderer/UI thread. Catalog events invalidate the derived value; no per-entry parallelism or limiter is relevant.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived automation array is cached until the next catalog signal, but local time-zone resolution is not cached within a projection. Warm reads without a catalog change reuse the derived value; every changed catalog performs N formatter constructions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the derived observable maps every entry, and the changed common guard invokes uncached Intl construction before preset discrimination.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical catalog size and formatter cost are not measured; this lowers severity, not confidence in the O(N) repeated construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression for larger catalogs; resolve the local zone once per projection batch.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or update a CRON automation from the dialog or configureAutomation tool
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Input is parsed and validated synchronously before approval/save. A successful action then follows the existing single automation-service mutation path and waits for authoritative Agent Host state; this mutation boundary remains the critical path to completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one AutomationCreateRequested or AutomationUpdateRequested action and await authoritative catalog state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC mutation per accepted create or update; no per-field or per-trigger fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preset automation creates and updates used the same single dispatch-and-wait boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The save/tool invocation waits for this response exactly as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the updated automation catalog/run state in Agent Host storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One batched persistence step per accepted mutation, not one write per CRON field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automation definitions were already validated and persisted through the same host mutation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host mutation completion includes persistence as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One schedule expression and one target per user/tool mutation. Target selection scans the already-loaded candidate session types; mutation cardinality remains one.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The tool/dialog issues one create or update. Agent Host mutations are serialized by the existing mutation tail and _dispatchAndWait waits for one authoritative catalog transition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Validation is cold and uncached, but occurs a bounded number of times for a tool proposal/save. Provider/catalog state is already loaded; no new cache key or negative-cache behavior is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unchanged boundary cardinality; the new CRON parsing is local synchronous CPU only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider response and storage latency vary, but the diff does not increase call count or concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional boundary fan-out or concurrency regression beyond the separately reported dialog typing work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Import or export an automation blueprint containing a CRON schedule
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Import reads one selected/dropped file before parsing YAML and validating CRON. Export converts one automation to YAML before writing one selected file; parsing/serialization is on the action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read blueprint file content before parse
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file read per import action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Blueprint import already performed one read before parse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Import waits for the read before parsing, unchanged by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file write per export action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Blueprint export already serialized and wrote one file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Export waits for this write, unchanged by the CRON support.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One blueprint document per import/export action and one bounded five-field schedule. No collection-wide fan-out was added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single user action awaits one read or write; there is no burst, queue, or new parallel operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Blueprint content and parsed schedules are not cached, consistent with one-shot file actions. Valid and invalid CRON inputs are validated once per parse; there is no repeated miss loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: callers show one read/write and the changed blueprint code adds only local validation/model support.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Document sizes are normally small and no new unbounded transformation is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; filesystem cardinality and serialization scale are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Evaluate schedules and claim due Agent Host automation runs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On definition validation or cursor initialization, nextAutomationCronOccurrence computes the next time. Warm scheduler ticks use persisted cursors; when a cursor is due or invalid, the mutation queue recomputes it, batches changed state into one persistence operation, then starts claimed runs through the existing execution service.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the batched next catalog and run state after claiming due schedules
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one batched persistence operation for a claim tick with changes, regardless of the number of changed automations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The scheduler already batched changed catalog/run state into one persistence call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence completes before changed state is published, matching prior scheduler behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/start the automation's execution session through the existing execution service
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One execution start per claimed automation run; sibling due triggers are coalesced into one run per automation per tick.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preset CRON-backed schedules used the same run claim and session execution path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Execution begins after claim/persistence; CRON grammar support does not add another session-start call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Catalog entries and schedule triggers scanned per claim tick; next-occurrence search depends on schedule sparsity. Effective computation remains one next-occurrence call per initialized/due/invalid schedule trigger, as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Claiming is serialized by _mutationTail. Due state changes are persisted in one batch; subsequent automation runs may overlap by existing design, but the diff does not increase run concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Persisted schedule cursors are the warm cache. Valid future cursors skip occurrence search; missing/invalid/due cursors recompute. The PR preserves this cache and search algorithm while sharing the parser and adding grammar/description support.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: runtime call sites, cursor checks, mutation serialization, coalescing, and batched persistence are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very sparse schedules can make the existing bounded ten-year search expensive, but that algorithm and coarse stepping predate this PR; newly accepted range-step syntax does not increase the bound or call frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No diff-introduced runtime scheduling regression or boundary fan-out; the runtime search mechanism is substantially unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 26 changed files and their relevant callers. Submitted two findings: repeated formatter-heavy synchronous work on each CRON edit, and per-entry local-time-zone formatter construction during catalog projection. Checked eager dialog allocation, parser/runtime scheduling, persistence, IPC mutation, blueprint filesystem paths, cache/cursor behavior, and concurrency; no additional high-confidence regressions or regression fixes were found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
